newsitem.title: USA: British skydiver takes first steps since accident.
newsitem.headline: British skydiver takes first steps since accident.

text.p: A novice British skydiver who miraculously survived a 12,000-foot (3,650 metres) drop with a failed parachute in Florida last weekend took his first steps on Thursday, two days after an operation on his fractured spine.

"He walked about eight to 10 feet (2-1/2 to 3 metres), he took his first steps," Joe Brown, a spokesman at Orlando Regional Medical Centre, told Reuters. He said the 21-year-old man, Gareth Griffith, underwent surgery on Tuesday following Sunday's accident.

"It was painful, very painful, but the expectation of course is that ... he will probably be out of here this time next week if he continues to progress. His physicians feel he should be able to take a regular commercial airliner back home," Brown added.
"He is very stable, he was taken out of intensive care yesterday (Wednesday) afternoon," he said.
Griffith, a management consultant from London, survived because his instructor sacrificed himself to break the young man's fall after his parachute did not open properly, witnesses said.
Griffith, a tourist making his first jump, also suffered injuries to his abdominal organs and several broken ribs. The injuries were not life threatening.
Instructor Michael Costello, 42, of Mount Dora, Florida, was killed instantly upon hitting the ground, police said.
Witness Lee Godwin said Costello saved his student by rolling at the last moment to take the brunt of the fall.

"An experienced skydiver's never going to lose his cool because it's not impossible to survive a fall like that," he said. "Mike kept his cool and did what he had to to save his student. That was Mike."
An instructor for 18 years, Costello was jumping in tandem with Griffith, a common practice for veterans jumping with novices, said Costello's business partner, Wilma Godwin.

The two were jumping into a field next to the rural airport in Umatilla, Florida, about 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Orlando. Griffith and five friends were enrolled in a two-week skydiving course, Godwin said.
